variants.headline: {{capital}} is no longer the largest city
body: {{largest}} has more residents than {{capital}}, according to the latest count, with {{largestPopulation}} people in its streets. While the capital remains the seat of {{terms.civic.government}}, its claim to the biggest population has ended.

variants.headline: No single largest city: {{largest}} level at {{largestPopulation}}
body: The latest count puts {{largest}} level at {{largestPopulation}} people, each with more people than {{capital}}. The capital keeps the government offices and the official title, but the population record now places it behind the leaders.

variants.headline: Population vs. Power
body: {{largest}} now holds {{largestPopulation}} residents, officially surpassing {{capital}} as the largest city in {{terms.civilization}}. While the {{terms.civic.government}} remains anchored in the capital, the economic heartbeat of the nation has migrated. As the center of gravity shifts, the nation must decide if power will follow the people or if {{capital}} can maintain its grip on the realm.

variants.headline: CAPITAL LOSES ITS CROWN
body: A tailor in {{largest}} just took an order for a hundred new banners. He doesn't care about the politics or the officials back in {{capital}}. {{largest}} is the new heart of the nation.

variants.headline: New population leader: {{largest}}
body: {{largest}} just became the biggest city in {{terms.civilization}}, surpassing {{capital}} with {{largestPopulation}} people. Check the full census report for the growth trends.

variants.headline: Widespread discontent over {{key}}
body: A common grievance has emerged across {{count}} cities in {{terms.civilization}}. Reports indicate that {{key}} is the primary source of unrest among the {{terms.civic.people}}.

variants.headline: One problem, {{count|city|cities}}
body: The entry {{key}} leads the complaint book in {{count}} of our cities, and a pattern that wide is policy by another name. Weather explains one bad season in one town; it does not explain the same line in every ledger. The {{terms.civic.government}} should be able to say when the choice was made and who expected to gain by it.

variants.headline: {{key}} in {{count}} cities
body: Bread lines are growing in {{count}} cities. The {{terms.civic.government}} seems to have forgotten we need to eat. Hang in there, {{terms.civic.people}}.

variants.headline: Boredom in {{count|city|cities}}
body: The complaint is the same in {{count}} of our cities: nothing to do once the day's work is done. Benches in the square fill before dark and empty by the first bell. A fiddler in one of those towns has played the same three songs all summer, and nobody has asked for a fourth.

variants.headline: Hunger tops the list in {{city}}
body: Famine is now the leading grievance in {{city}}, and {{faminePopulation}} {{terms.civic.people}} are unhappy. Bread lines form before sunrise, and the ovens go cold by noon. As the city has not announced new grain shipments, the square empties as soon as the last loaf is sold.

variants.headline: Why {{city}} is hungry
body: {{city}} cannot feed itself, and the city's own count puts famine ahead of every other grievance. {{faminePopulation}} {{terms.civic.people}} are unhappy because of it. Granaries do not empty on their own; someone set the harvest, the stores and the roads, and someone should explain the result.

variants.headline: Empty stalls in {{city}}
body: A woman in {{city}} keeps a chipped bowl by her door for the bread cart. Last winter the cart came twice a day; now it comes once and is empty before she reaches the corner. She has stopped hurrying, she says, because hurrying does not bake bread.

variants.headline: Notice to the {{terms.civic.people}} of {{city}}
body: We are informed that {{faminePopulation}} souls in {{city}} now suffer the trial of hunger. Let the faithful gather at the shrines to pray for providence, that the heavens may grant us relief from this scarcity.

variants.headline: A {{milestone}} at last: {{city}} passes {{population}}
body: The count in {{city}} now stands at {{population}} people, making it a {{milestone}}. The newest lane is still muddy, but new families have already moved in. City officials say markets stays busy all day long, straining all kinds of public infrastructure.

variants.headline: The Weight of Growth in {{cityName}}
body: The census is in: {{city}} is now a {{milestone}} with {{population}} residents. While the numbers signal a triumph of expansion, the city's appetite for better amenities is ever growing faster. It is up to {{owner.civic.government}} to provide for its people and lead the world.

variants.headline: Notice of population growth in {{cityName}}
body: Hear me, {{terms.civic.people}}! {{city}} has passed {{population}} people and is officially a {{milestone}}! Our borders expand and our power grows. {{cityName}} is a {{milestone}}!

variants.headline: {{cityName}} Declared a {{milestone}}
body: {{city}} now numbers {{population}} souls, officially qualifying it as a {{milestone}}. In this era of sudden expansion, we must hope that the virtues of our fathers are not lost amidst the ever-shifting fashions of a modern city.

variants.headline: Starvation reported in {{city}}
body: The food supply in {{city}} has fallen to critical levels. With only {{foodStored}} remaining and a deficit of {{shortfall}} per turn, the population is suffering from hunger.

variants.headline: Why {{city}} is starving in peacetime
body: There is no siege at {{city}}, no raiders in the fields and no enemy at the gate. Yet the city loses {{shortfall}} of food a day from a store of {{foodStored}}, and the granary books say so plainly. Peacetime hunger is somebody's decision, and somebody should be asked to explain it.

variants.headline: The granary at {{city}} is emptying
body: A baker on the high street in {{city}} now cuts every loaf in two before she opens the shop. The granary that feeds her ovens holds {{foodStored}} of grain and loses {{shortfall}} of that a day. She has stopped taking orders for next week, and her customers have stopped asking.

variants.headline: A Dire Account from {{city}}
body: We are credibly informed that a severe dearth has befallen the people of {{city}}, though no enemy army invests the walls to block our trade.
Current Stores: {{foodStored}}; Daily Shortfall: {{shortfall}}
The {{terms.civic.government}} continues to speak of national prosperity, yet this tally reveals a tragedy of administrative neglect.

variants.headline: Celebrations begin in {{city}}
body: A public celebration has begun in {{city}}. Residents have gathered in the streets to mark the occasion with festivities.

variants.headline: Public festivities in {{city}}
body: A celebration has commenced within the walls of {{city}}. All {{terms.civic.people}} are encouraged to join in the merrymaking.
